authoredBy: Antigravity — Story Bible for The Island of Missing Trees (Elif Shafak)

world.era: Contemporary dual timeline: 1974 Nicosia (divided Cyprus during civil war/partition) and late 2010s North London (suburban exile and storm Hera)
world.setting: A dual-world narrative: The war-torn, sun-baked alleys of divided Nicosia centered around The Happy Fig tavern, contrasted with a stormy, winter-frozen suburban North London garden where an immigrant botanist buries a cutting beneath the English earth.
world.register: literary drama / ecological memory / transgenerational trauma

narrator.name: Narrator / The Fig Tree
narrator.look: A sentient ecological observer and literary host reflecting on transgenerational memory and botanical resilience across decades of civil conflict.

kostas.name: Kostas Kazantzakis
kostas.look: Greek Cypriot botanist and evolutionary ecologist, quiet, scientific, grieving his late wife while tending his North London garden.

defne.name: Defne
defne.look: Turkish Cypriot woman with deep, expressive dark eyes and dark curly hair; an archaeologist working for the Committee on Missing Persons.

ada.name: Ada Kazantzakis
ada.look: Sixteen-year-old British-Cypriot high school student in North London with dark shoulder-length hair and an intense, wounded posture.

meryem.name: Aunt Meryem
meryem.look: Defne's vibrant, volatile Turkish sister arriving from Cyprus with colorful patterned dresses, bold jewelry, and suitcase full of spices and superstitions.

yiorgos.name: Yiorgos
yiorgos.look: Greek taverna owner of The Happy Fig, warm, hospitable, with a thick moustache, working alongside Yusuf to shelter lovers in a divided city.

yusuf.name: Yusuf
yusuf.look: Turkish taverna co-owner of The Happy Fig, gentle, thoughtful, culinary partner of Yiorgos creating a peaceful culinary haven.

everyman.name: The Observer
everyman.look: The outside reader probing the anatomy of inherited silence, civil war partitions, and transgenerational grief.

classroom.look: The stifling, fluorescent-lit North London classroom where Ada's 52-second scream goes viral.

cafe.look: The Happy Fig taverna in Nicosia with its lush fig tree growing through the roof, hanging herbs, and clandestine candlelit tables.

room.look: The quiet, sterile London home filled with unspoken memories and unaddressed grief.

kitchen.look: The suburban London kitchen transformed by Meryem's aromatic Mediterranean cooking and traditional dishes.

forest.look: The cold suburban garden trench in winter and the wild Mediterranean flora of Cyprus.

street.look: The divided streets of Nicosia with barbed wire and military checkpoints.

horizon.look: The Mediterranean coastline of Cyprus and the overcast skies of London awaiting Storm Hera.

abstract.look: The conceptual space of subterranean root networks, historical trauma, and silence.

signatureObjects.name: Buried Fig Tree Cutting
signatureObjects.why: Kostas trenches and buries the cutting from Cyprus in North London to protect it from frost, an exact physical manifestation of buried migrant memory.

signatureObjects.name: The Deep Well and Oil Tin
signatureObjects.why: The tragic mass grave where Yiorgos and Yusuf were chained and sunk with a concrete-filled oil tin, discovered by the Committee on Missing Persons.

spine.claim: Ada's viral classroom scream in North London and the mystery of buried migrant grief.
The sanctuary of The Happy Fig in 1974 Nicosia and the forbidden love across ethnic lines.
Civil conflict, the destruction of the taverna, and the excavation of missing persons' graves.
Aunt Meryem's arrival in London, culinary reclamation, and breaking the family's code of silence.
The unearthing of the buried fig tree as Storm Hera breaks, proving ecological memory outlasts borders.
